decision: The language-neutral data-architecture rules (Core Principles 1-7, the anti-pattern list, the Instructions checklist, the analyse-refactor-verify Workflow with its state file, the define-the-types preference order and the generic rationalizations) live once in coding-data-architecture, which routes Python to coding-python-data-architecture and Rust to coding-rust-data-architecture; the language skills hold only mechanisms.

evidence.text: Heading diff of the pre-rename Python skill against the two new files: every heading is present in one of them except the renamed H1; a line-level check of the pre-edit text listed 85 non-verbatim lines, each reviewed as reworded or moved into a Python section. Probes in checklist-20261109-generic-skill.md.

reopen_if: A language skill needs a different workflow or principle numbering than the generic skill holds, or readers of a language skill repeatedly act without loading the generic one.
why: The Python skill was the only home of rules that hold in any language, so a reader working in another language had no skill to load; copying them into each language skill would let the copies drift.

anchors: One case is a boundary, not a shim: a wire format the system MUST still read
decision: Core Principle 7 keeps its ban on compatibility shims and names one boundary case: a wire format the system must still read gets its own versioned wire record, converted once into the domain type, and old-format aliases and defaults live on that record only. A format nothing reads any more is deleted. The rule is stated once here; the Rust skill points at it.

evidence.text: checklist-20261109-review-fixes.md: RED (opus, pre-edit text) reported four contradictions on a persisted v1/v2 scenario and answered the retirement question NONE; GREEN (opus, edited text) quoted Principle 7's boundary case and the Rust pointer, found no contradiction, and answered 'deleted' from the text.

reopen_if: A reviewer meets an old-format reader that is not at a boundary (an alias kept inside domain code) and the boundary case is cited to justify it.
why: The Rust skill prescribed versioned DTOs carrying serde alias and default while Principle 7 forbade aliases and layers accepting old formats, and the Rust skill also said default must never make an old payload parse; a reader had two contradicting rules and no precedence.
